document_check.note: The document is Wu P, Lv Z, Bi Y et al. (2024) 'Network-based statistics reveals an enhanced subnetwork in prefrontal cortex in mild cognitive impairment: a functional near-infrared spectroscopy study', Front. Aging Neurosci. 16:1416816. Authors, year and design (cross-sectional resting-state fNIRS, 67 MCI vs 71 HC) match the citation, and the document reports increased prefrontal connectivity that the authors say may reflect compensation.

cited_result: Higher resting-state prefrontal fNIRS functional connectivity (a right-PFC subnetwork: Ch12-Ch15, Ch12-Ch16, Ch13-Ch15, Ch13-Ch16) in MCI than in healthy controls, which the authors say may reflect cognitive compensation.
tool_reason: The cited result compares a biomarker (fNIRS connectivity) between MCI and control groups measured at a single time point, and the authors themselves describe the design as cross-sectional.

domains.domain: Item 1: Criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined
domains.rationale: Inclusion and exclusion criteria for all participants and additional criteria for MCI are stated.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: All participants met the following inclusion criteria: (1) aged 55 years or above; (2) no clinical diagnosis of AD; (3) right-handedness.

domains.domain: Item 2: Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: The setting (community participants in Nanning) and demographics (Table 1) are reported. How participants were recruited and over what period are not, and the 26 of 164 exclusions (incomplete assessment or channel CV > 15%) are not broken down by group.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: A total of 164 participants were enrolled from local communities in Nanning City, China. After excluding participants who did not complete the cognitive assessments and those with data quality issues (channel signal coefficient of variation >15%), a final sample of 138 participants was included.

domains.domain: Item 3: Exposure measured in a valid and reliable way
domains.rationale: Here the exposure is group membership (MCI vs control), assessed with the validated Chinese MoCA, given the same way to everyone before fNIRS.

signalling.question: Was the exposure (group assignment) measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Cognitive assessments were conducted using the Chinese version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), with a maximum score of 30.

domains.domain: Item 4: Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: MCI is defined by subjective complaint plus education-stratified MoCA cut-offs. That is a screening-score definition, not a clinical diagnosis: no clinician work-up and no assessment of daily function are reported. No criteria are stated for the healthy controls, and their mean MoCA of 24.63 (SD 2.49) implies some controls near or below the MCI cut-off. The paper adds 1 point for education under 12 years and also applies education-stratified cut-offs, and it is unclear whether both adjustments were applied together.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition (MCI)?
signalling.quote: MCI patients had to meet the following requirements: (1) presence of subjective memory complaints; (2) according to Chinese MoCA norms (Lu et al., 2011), MoCA scores of ≤13 for illiterate individuals, ≤19 for individuals with 1–6 years of education, and ≤ 24 for individuals with 7 or more years of education.

signalling.question: Were criteria for the control group stated?
signalling.quote: Searched Methods 2.1 and Table 1 for control-group definition or MoCA threshold; only 'age-, gender-, and education-matched healthy individuals' and HC MoCA '24.63 ± 2.49' are reported.

signalling.question: Was the MoCA education correction applied consistently with the stratified cut-offs?
signalling.quote: For participants with <12 years of education, 1 point was added to their MoCA total score.

domains.rationale: Age, sex and education are named as matching factors, and psychiatric, neurological and systemic disease and medication use are handled by exclusion.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: The final sample comprised 67 patients with MCI and 71 age-, gender-, and education-matched healthy individuals.

signalling.question: Were other potential confounders addressed?
signalling.quote: Exclusion criteria consisted of: (1) comorbid psychiatric or neurological disorders, as well as other systemic diseases; (2) severe impairments in vision or hearing, or conditions such as age-related cataracts that would hinder participant cooperation; (3) history of using antipsychotic medications or substance abuse.

domains.domain: Item 6: Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated
domains.rationale: Groups were frequency matched and shown not to differ on the demographic confounders. The connectivity comparison itself is unadjusted, which is acceptable given the matching.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: No significant statistical difference was found in gender, age, and education level between the two groups (p > 0.05).

domains.domain: Item 7: Outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way
domains.rationale: The same portable device, 10/20 probe placement, 8-minute eyes-closed rest and standard Homer2 pipeline were used for everyone. The paper reports no short-separation regression of systemic physiology, and it names low spatial resolution and limited depth as limitations.

signalling.question: Was the outcome (prefrontal functional connectivity) measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: The preprocessing of fNIRS data was carried out using the Homer2 toolkit on the Matlab 17.0 platform (Huppert et al., 2009).

signalling.question: Was acquisition standardised across participants?
signalling.quote: During the study, fNIRS signals were collected from participants during an 8-min resting period. Throughout the data acquisition process, participants were instructed to maintain a comfortable sitting position, close their eyes, relax, and avoid any excessive head movements.

domains.rationale: Group differences in 276 connections were tested with FDR-corrected t-tests and with network-based statistics (5,000 permutations), which control multiplicity appropriately.

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: The first method employed independent samples t-tests with FDR correction, and a significance level of p < 0.05 was used to indicate a statistical difference. The second method involved employing the NBS approach, implemented using the NBS 1.2 toolbox in Matlab 17.0.

signalling.question: Was the permutation procedure described?
signalling.quote: A t-test was performed on each connection, with a p-value threshold of 0.05 and 5,000 permutations.

overall: Some concerns (7 of 8 items Yes; item 4 Unclear)
overall_rationale: Confounder identification, confounder strategy, outcome measurement and analysis are all adequate, so the review's high-risk rule is not triggered. MCI is classified only by subjective complaint and MoCA cut-offs, with no stated criteria for controls, so the condition item is unclear. That misclassification risk keeps the result at some concerns rather than low.
